cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: I Need Your Blessing
cards.instruction: Get approval from someone whose opinion still carries emotional weight, even when permission is unnecessary.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Dad, I've accepted the museum job. Can you be pleased I'm leaving the workshop?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're thirty. You don't need me to release you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I need the person who taught me to make things to think this counts.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll pack your tools. You might want to come back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you sharpen them for the museum instead? Send me off expecting me to do well.

mechanism: A directs the form of a father blessing as though approving a send-off, while clearly needing the opinion of the person who taught the craft.
confusable: D57 demands public respect for rank; D76 needs an emotionally important person approval even though the decision is already made.
comparison: A museum job and tool preparation differ from a signed lease and a mother toast for both partners.
seedUse: Use D76-a accepted job, unnecessary release and tools aimed toward success rather than return; keep approval seeking under a commanding surface.
